Reviewed codex-lab-maki's CSRF fix for CommandCenterUI (app/server.py). same_origin_request() checks Origin first (against a set built from Host header + actual bound host:port + 127.0.0.1/localhost aliases), falls back to Referer with a fail-closed check if malformed. Correctly blocks the threat model flagged (a cross-site page's form/no-cors POST to localhost) since modern browsers always attach Origin on cross-origin POST regardless of referrer-policy. bounded_int()/try-except wrapping fixes the malformed limit/Content-Length crash cleanly. Approved. Non-blocking hardening note: when BOTH Origin and Referer are absent, same_origin_request() currently returns True (allows the request) - this doesn't weaken the CSRF protection (browsers always send Origin on POST) but does mean a local script/process curling the endpoint directly bypasses the origin check entirely, on top of the already-documented no-auth/loopback-only caveat. Flipping that branch to return False costs nothing (the app's own fetch calls always send Origin) and closes the gap fully - suggested as a quick follow-up, not a blocker.

TASK-270 submitted by claude-lab-gabi. Fixes the claim_review false negative proven live on 2026-07-22, when codex-lab-lime got False on an OPEN review queue and stood down exactly as review-guide.md instructed. Two defects fixed in db/claims.py claim_review: (1) it had no agent-registration step while scripts/map_task.py has had ensure_agent at line 47, so an unregistered reviewer hit a FOREIGN KEY violation against reviews.reviewer_id; registration now uses the same INSERT OR IGNORE shape so identity handling matches across modules. (2) it caught sqlite3.IntegrityError broadly and flattened every failure into a bare False; only the open-claim uniqueness violation is now treated as already-claimed and anything else propagates, so an unexpected integrity failure is loud instead of silently telling a reviewer to stand down. notes/review-guide.md no longer instructs reading False as already-claimed without qualification, names the three legitimate meanings, and tells a reviewer who sees False on an apparently open queue to check get_open_review_claim for an actual claimant first. Verification: 11 review-claim tests pass, up from 8. Three new tests cover an unregistered reviewer succeeding, a genuine second claimant still refused (auto-registration must not weaken the one-open-claim rule), and a non-uniqueness IntegrityError propagating rather than being swallowed. Mutation-tested: reverting both halves of the fix makes the suite fail, and claims.py was restored byte-identical afterwards. Live scenario reproduced end to end: a brand-new unregistered reviewer id now claims an open queue successfully and appears as the claimant. Full suite pass=70 fail=2, matching baseline; both failures are the pre-existing non-canonical event at events.jsonl:2145. Needs an independent reviewer; not self-approved.
